@graph.name: FHIR R4 JSON
@graph.description: The Cascade Bridge Adapter for FHIR R4 JSON: the package of data a Cascade Bridge runs to turn FHIR R4 resources, alone or as the entries of a Bundle, into Cascade records. Import-only. This crate is the adapter's manifest: a Bridge reads the root entity first, for the format id, the source media type, the source schema, the two envelopes, the detect rule, the document table queries, the mappings, the findings queries and the table they read, the profile the Bridge must offer, the vocabulary repository and the paths, in it, of the ontology and shapes files the adapter is read against, the gap scheme every finding takes its body from, each gap declaring the sh:resultSeverity its findings carry where that is not sh:Info, the source accounting, and the test manifest. The data entities carry provenance for every committed file, and a sha256 computed locally over the committed bytes of each digested one. Twenty-seven inputs are copied byte for byte from the conformance repository's fixtures/clinical-fhir at the commit isBasedOn names; the others are authored here, and each says so.

@graph.name: bundle
@graph.description: A Bundle: each entry is a record, so its fullUrl stays with its resource; docs/format.md, "The two envelopes".

@graph.name: resource
@graph.description: A resource alone: the document is the record.

@graph.name: sparql-1.1
@graph.description: Declared in the Cascade Bridge Specification's vocabulary, vocab/bridge.ttl in cascade-bridge-spec.

@graph.name: Cascade Bridge Adapter profile
@graph.description: The RO-Crate 1.2 Profile Crate a conforming adapter package names in conformsTo; the Profile Crate describing it is adapter/profile/ro-crate-metadata.json in cascade-bridge-spec.

@graph.name: cascade-vocabulary
@graph.description: The repository the adapter's vocabularies are read from, at the version a run picks; the paths in bridge:vocabularyFile are read there. A web-based data entity, referenced and not committed: the RO-Crate 1.2 validator reads every SoftwareSourceCode as a script that must be a File in hasPart.

@graph.description: One of the vocabularies the adapter writes, as cascade-vocabulary declares it.

@graph.description: One of the vocabularies the adapter writes, as cascade-vocabulary declares it.

@graph.description: One of the vocabularies the adapter writes, as cascade-vocabulary declares it.

@graph.name: FHIR R4 JSON Schema, pinned copy
@graph.description: HL7's JSON Schema for FHIR R4, pinned byte for byte: the source schema every record is validated against. Identical to the file at the isBasedOn URL on 2026-09-27; sha256 is computed locally over the committed bytes. Never edited; to change it, replace it from its source and update contentSize and sha256 in the same commit.

@graph.name: FHIR R4 JSON Schema
@graph.description: HL7's published JSON Schema for FHIR R4 (4.0.1), draft-06, its id http://hl7.org/fhir/json-schema/4.0. Downloaded over HTTPS on 2026-09-27; dateModified is the HTTPS Last-Modified. HL7 publishes no digest beside it; the copy inside fhir.schema.json.zip on the same site, read the same day, has the same sha256.

@graph.name: Detect rule
@graph.description: The detect rule, bridge:detectQuery: an ASK over the envelope skeleton, true for a JSON document whose value is a FHIR resource, a Bundle among them.

@graph.name: Document table
@graph.description: A bridge:documentTableQuery: for each record, where it stands and its resource's type, id and fullUrl, so record.rq tells an id or a urn:uuid the document repeats and resolves a reference to another record of the document.

@graph.name: Document table: which Observations are lab results
@graph.description: A bridge:documentTableQuery: a row for each Observation of a record that is a lab result, wherever it stands, by its category, or, where it has none, by a LOINC code no vital sign of vocab/fhir-vital-signs.ttl carries, a panel excluded; record.rq, lab-result.rq and the findings queries ask it whether one is.

@graph.name: Document table: Medications and the references to them
@graph.description: A bridge:documentTableQuery: a row for each Medication of a record, wherever it stands, with its id, its name and its RxNorm codes, and a row for each medication's reference to one, so that medication.rq reads a drug a reference names from the record holding it, and resource-type-findings.rq leaves out a Medication something references.

@graph.name: Mapping: records, versions and arrivals
@graph.description: For each resource of a mapped type, the record's own and each it contains: the record, named by the Cascade Bridge Specification's naming convention from the server, type and id, the urn:uuid fullUrl, the containing record's name and the local id, or the document and the record's selector; its class, its source URL where its name has one, and its source id; its version, the patient the version is about, and the version's arrival with the resource's meta.versionId and meta.lastUpdated.

@graph.name: Mapping: an AllergyIntolerance's version
@graph.description: What an AllergyIntolerance says, written on the version record.rq names: allergen, allergen codes, clinical and verification status, type, criticality, category, onset, reactions, their codes and severity, and notes.

@graph.name: Mapping: a Condition's version
@graph.description: What a Condition says, written on the version record.rq names: name, SNOMED CT and ICD-10-CM codes, clinical and verification status, category, onset, abatement and notes.

@graph.name: Mapping: an Immunization's version
@graph.description: What an Immunization says, written on the version record.rq names: vaccine name and CVX code, date, status, lot number, dose, route, site and notes.

@graph.name: Mapping: a Procedure's version
@graph.description: What a Procedure says, written on the version record.rq names: name, SNOMED CT and CPT codes, date and status.

@graph.name: Mapping: a Patient's version
@graph.description: What a Patient says, written on the version record.rq names: the first name it states, and its birth date.

@graph.name: Mapping: a MedicationRequest's or MedicationStatement's version
@graph.description: What a medication says, written on the version record.rq names: its intent, prescribed for a request and reportedUse for a statement; the drug's name and RxNorm codes, from its concept or from the Medication its reference resolves to in the document, else the reference's display; status, start and end dates, and the first dosage's text.

@graph.name: Mapping: a lab result's version
@graph.description: What a lab result says, written on the version record.rq names: test name and LOINC codes, value as the source wrote it and its unit, reference range, interpretation, performed time and status.

@graph.name: Findings: a resource of a type this release does not map
@graph.description: A finding for each resource, the record's own or one it contains, whose type is not one of the five this release maps.

@graph.name: Findings: a document of a FHIR version other than R4
@graph.description: A finding for each record of a document whose supplied bridge:sourceFormatVersion is not an R4 version; the mappings write nothing for it.

@graph.name: Findings: an id the document repeats
@graph.description: A finding for each record whose resource's type and id, or whose urn:uuid fullUrl, another record of the document holds too, so record.rq names it from the document and its selector.

@graph.name: Findings: a recorded date
@graph.description: A finding for each AllergyIntolerance or Condition that states the date it was recorded, which no Cascade predicate carries.

@graph.name: Findings: a reference's display
@graph.description: A finding for each patient, subject or reason reference of a mapped resource that carries a display string, which no Cascade predicate carries.

@graph.name: Findings: an Observation that is not a lab result
@graph.description: Reports fhirr4:observationNotLabResult for each Observation lab-result-table.rq does not call a lab result, at what decided it: a category, a vital sign's LOINC code, the type of one with neither category nor LOINC code, or a panel's members.

@graph.name: Findings: a medication's unresolved reference and its note
@graph.description: Reports fhirr4:medicationOutsideDocument for a medication's reference to a Medication its document does not hold, and fhirr4:medicationNote for a medication's note, which the source accounting carries at the same path for the other kinds.

@graph.name: FHIR R4 JSON source accounting
@graph.description: The file the crate names as bridge:sourceAccounting: one bridge:PathEntry for each path a mapping in in/sparql/ reads and each path the judged inputs carry, written as JSON Pointer reference tokens from the record, at every place a resource stands in one: the record under the resource envelope, /resource under the Bundle envelope, and /contained under either; each with its verdict against in/sparql/.

@graph.name: Findings: a patient reference in a document from no known server
@graph.description: A finding for each patient or subject reference of a mapped resource written relative to a server, in a document supplied no bridge:serverBaseUrl: it names no record, and record.rq writes no link for it.

@graph.name: FHIR R4 JSON gaps
@graph.description: The scheme every finding this adapter reports takes its body from: one skos:Concept per gap, in this adapter's own namespace (https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/adapter/fhir-r4/v1-draft#), each under one of the bridge:gapKinds the Cascade Bridge Specification declares.

@graph.name: FHIR R4 vital signs
@graph.description: The bridge:table lab-result-table.rq and observation-findings.rq read to tell a vital sign from a lab result when an Observation carries no category: one skos:Concept per LOINC code of the table of vital signs in FHIR R4's vital signs profile, its skos:notation the code. Transcribed from the isBasedOn page, read on 2026-10-06. Not a concept map: no code maps to a Cascade term, and no entry of the source accounting looks a value up in it.

@graph.name: Criticality as allergy severity
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes AllergyIntolerance.criticality as health:allergySeverity, high as severe, low as mild, unable-to-assess as moderate, where no reaction states a severity; read back as clinical:criticality.

@graph.name: Dates widened
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a FHIR date as an xsd:dateTime at T00:00:00Z (onset, abatement, administration, performed, a medication's start and end); the suffix is read off. A birth date stays an xsd:date.

@graph.name: Vaccine code prefixed
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a CVX code prefixed CVX-, as CVX-141; read as the code alone.

@graph.name: Snomed code as iri
@graph.description: A SNOMED CT code written as an IRI in http://snomed.info/sct/ is read as the code alone, on both sides: the adapter's health:snomedCode is an IRI, its clinical:snomedCode a string.

@graph.name: Unknown placeholders
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes Unknown Condition, Unknown Medication and their like where a resource carries no code, and an interpretation of unknown where a lab result states none; read as absent.

@graph.name: Predicate renames
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes health:abatementDate, clinical:procedureStatus, clinical:performedDate, clinical:procedureSnomedCode and cascade:profileId where the adapter writes clinical:abatementDate, clinical:status, clinical:procedureDate, clinical:snomedCode and cascade:sourceRecordId; and, of a medication, health:startDate, health:endDate and health:sourceRecordId where the adapter writes clinical:startDate, clinical:endDate and clinical:sourceRecordId.

@graph.name: Never written
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes no allergen code, no recorded date and no patient name, so those fields are not compared.

@graph.name: Merges id less entries
@graph.description: cascade-cli names identical id-less entries of one Bundle as one subject, and the entries of a Bundle repeating an id as one subject; the adapter names a record for each.

@graph.name: Drops contained
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes no record for a contained resource.

@graph.name: LOINC code with a hash
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a LOINC code as an IRI in http://loinc.org/rdf#, where step 2 of jayostis/cascade-runtime-js#70 and the adapter write http://loinc.org/rdf/; read as the code alone.

@graph.name: Numbers reprinted
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a lab result's value and its reference range's bounds as JavaScript prints the parsed number, 6.8 for 6.80 and 4 for 4.0; the adapter writes the number as the document writes it. Read as numbers.

@graph.name: Medication reference unresolved
@graph.description: cascade-cli names a medication whose drug is a contained Medication or another entry of its Bundle Unknown Medication, with no RxNorm code; the adapter reads the Medication's name and codes. Those fields are not compared for those inputs.

@graph.name: Vital signs as records
@graph.description: cascade-cli writes a vital-sign Observation as a clinical:VitalSign record; the adapter writes none and reports fhirr4:observationNotLabResult. No view reads it.
